theorem_general_root_string.setup: Let g_S be the ORIGINAL Chevalley-Serre algebra for the displayed A(r,s), with r,s positive integers and its formal Z^3 simple-root grading. Put E=ad(e_3), F=ad(f_3), H=ad(h_3). For a homogeneous x of formal degree (a,b,n), Hx=m x with m=2n-r a-s b. This remains true when the Cartan matrix is singular, because the formal grading, not injectivity of the numerical Cartan-weight map, is used.
theorem_general_root_string.claim: If m>0, F is injective on the entire homogeneous degree-(a,b,n) subspace of g_S. Equivalently any nonzero homogeneous x killed by F has m=-N for some nonnegative integer N. When m=0, Fx=0 additionally forces Ex=0. These statements do not require x to be lowest for the finite Levi or PBW-primitive.
proof: E is locally nilpotent on g_S. On each e_i, i not 3, the defining positive Serre relation makes a power of E zero; E(e_3)=0. On f_i, i not 3, E(f_i)=0; E(f_3)=h_3, E^2(f_3)=-2e_3, E^3(f_3)=0. For every Cartan h, E^2(h)=0. Thus E is nilpotent on every generator of g_S. By the derivation Leibniz rule, a sufficiently high power of E kills every finite Lie word, and hence every element. No property of an additional maximal/minimal quotient is assumed.
The Chevalley relations give [H,E]=2E, [H,F]=-2F and [E,F]=H. If Fx=0 and Hx=m x, induction from [F,E]=-H yields F(E^k x)=-k(m+k-1)E^(k-1)x for every integer k>=1.

Suppose x is nonzero. Local nilpotence lets N be the largest nonnegative integer with E^N x nonzero. Setting k=N+1 in the displayed identity gives 0=-(N+1)(m+N)E^N x. Characteristic zero gives m=-N<=0. Thus m>0 and Fx=0 force x=0. If m=0, then N=0, so Ex=0. This is a proof by the full symbolic root string, not a selected parameter or numerical control probe.

proof: A vector in the original ordinary critical-lowest D_3 kernel has formal degree (a,b,5) and is killed by ad(f_3). The original algebra's h_3-eigenvalue on it is 10-r a-s b. Under the strict inequality, the root-string lemma forces the vector to be zero. This works in the ACTUAL full Serre quotient, including every target relation, rather than in the free source alone.

By finite-Levi semisimplicity and the established Q1/Q2 lowest-line identification, zero lowest kernel is exactly M_mu(K)=0. Apply the exact sequence 0 -> M_mu(F_free/G) -> M_mu(K) -> M_mu(L) -> 0. Both end multiplicity spaces therefore vanish separately. Equivalently the mu-isotypic free annihilator is contained in the full actual I, and the mu-isotypic part of D(C) intersect J equals the mu-isotypic part of D(I). No claim about other mu or a non-isotypic full inclusion is made.

For any actual Y contained in J, T=(D(C) intersect Y)/(D(I) intersect Y) injects into L by inclusion: its kernel is precisely D(I) intersect Y. Hence M_mu(T)=0 in this same strict region. The full denominator D(I) intersect Y is retained throughout; it is not replaced by D(Z).
